title: Moving parts in the Design page
ask: Should the Design page let you move a part and save its place into the record, or do you give placements in chat?
why: You asked to view the harness in 3D and play with it for fine tuning (D-514). Every place in the scene today is provisional - no row places the units, the PMU, the dash post or any far end - and the export puts them by fractions of the dash zone box. A place you set in the app would become the row the export reads (a place column on the electrical parts, typed only through your answer, like any other), and the scene would then show the design where you put it, until the car is measured and a measurement replaces it. Whether the app gets that mode is scope and how the page feels, so it is yours.
options:
(a) Move by steps: tap a part, nudge it 1, 10 or 100 mm and 5 degrees with buttons or arrow keys, and press Save place; the app writes an answer, a run applies it. About a day of app work; precise on the phone; forecloses nothing.
(b) Free drag with the pointer or finger, then the same Save place. More work, less precise on a phone, and easy to knock a part by accident.
(c) No moving in the app: you say placements in chat or answer a block per part, and the export reads the row. Costs nothing now; every tweak is a message.
recommend: (a), unless you would rather measure the dash first and never place by eye - then (c).
stops: The move-and-save mode in the app (a later 02-APP row) and the place column on the electrical parts; the scene keeps its provisional places meanwhile.

title: The CUR's connection to the harness - two leads, sixteen lines
ask: Does the CUR get two sealed receptacles on its back (one per lead, like the CU), one receptacle with the wink lead through a grommet, or a grommet alone?
why: The left plate's board has two leads: J1, twelve lines to the CU's DP-DCU-E (D-492), and J2, the wink lead's four lines to the dash post (D-504) - sixteen conductors. The earlier block 01.40 offered one DT13-12PA receptacle for both; the CUR mock-up's own check refused that (twelve ways cannot carry sixteen conductors), so that block is replaced by this one. As the Control Unit Remote - a sealed mini unit like the CU (D-514) - the leads leave its box by a receptacle each, by one receptacle and a grommet, or by a grommet alone. A receptacle is a part bought, so the choice is yours. The mock-up builds every option on one parameter and shows the recommended one until you answer.
options:
(a) Two receptacles on the CUR's back: a DT13-12PA for J1 and a DT13-06PA for J2, with a plug kit for each - about 25 USD; the CUR comes out of the dash with nothing attached, exactly like the CU; the box grows about 1.5 mm wider.
(b) One DT13-12PA for J1, and J2's wink lead through a sealed grommet beside it - about 15 USD; the CUR comes out with the wink lead trailing to the dash post.
(c) One sealed grommet, both leads captive - nothing bought; the CUR comes out with both leads and their plugs trailing.
recommend: (a), unless 10 USD and one more plug matter more to you than the CUR unplugging as clean as the CU.
stops: The CUR's rear plate detail and its parts rows; the mock-up shows the two receptacles until you answer.
